display.title: Torah, the Best Thing of All, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: On a ship full of merchants boasting of gold, silver and diamonds, Rabbi Akiva says he carries a treasure worth more than all of it, which no one can take from him.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with Dovid HaMelech's words in Tehillim, that the Torah is better than thousands of gold and silver: wealth can be taken away, but Torah that you have learned stays locked in your mind and heart forever. Rabbi Akiva is traveling by sea on a large boat full of wealthy businessmen, who have no interest in learning with him. Each evening on deck they boast about their merchandise: one has gold nuggets, another silver, a third opens a box of sparkling diamonds. When they mockingly ask the rabbi what he brought, Rabbi Akiva smiles and says his treasure is worth more than all the gold and silver in the world, that he needs no hiding place, and that he takes it with him wherever he goes. The merchants laugh and go off to check their hidden goods. The chapter ends with a promise that the merchants are in for a big surprise.
display.lesson: Torah learning is a treasure that can never be taken away.
